title: fix(objectql, plugin-auth)!: organization delete refuses while records remain, removes its own auth structure as one unit, and never orphans a tenant column
body:
Fixes #24948
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

Executes the maintainer's ruling on #24948 (letter B, record 6303358360), against the measurement 6297602613 and the claim 6303408016. Also executes the seat decisions 6305179819 (append-only ledgers exempt and kept; business units, positions, sharing rules and settings stay records; the deviations accepted), 6305996369 (the answers to contract review 6305988777, addressed item by item below) 6307135388 (option B: engine-owned rows are treated like the ledgers; see **Round 4** below) and 6307815346 (the declaration decides, with no per-table exceptions). It also answers delta review 6308041940 (**Round 5** below).

## What changes

**1. Refused while the organization owns records, before anything is deleted.** `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/delete` answers `409` with the standard `DELETE_RESTRICTED` code and `dependents: [{ object, count }]`, one entry per table that still names the organization in its tenant column. It carries counts only, never a row value.
- The refusal runs in better-auth's global `hooks.before`, ahead of the vendor handler, so a refused delete writes nothing, the caller's active organization included.
- It runs only for a caller the vendor itself would admit (a member whose role holds `organization: ['delete']`, asked of the vendor's own `hasPermission`), so a caller the vendor refuses gets the vendor's 403 and no count.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts:2453` (the `hooks.before` branch), `:8122` (`assertOrganizationDeletable`); `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/organization-delete.ts:134` (`organizationDeleteRefusal`).

**2. The organization's own auth structure goes with it.** Measured on a booted showcase: a door-created organization owns 1 `sys_member`, 1 `sys_team`, 1 `sys_team_member` and 1 `sys_user_permission_set`, and nothing else. The creator's session also names it, through `active_organization_id`, which is a pointer, not a tenant column.

| Table | How it names the organization | Removed by |
|---|---|---|
| `sys_member` | `organization_id`, `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-member.object.ts:312` | better-auth `adapter.deleteOrganization` (better-auth 1.7.3 `dist/plugins/organization/adapter.mjs:370-395`) |
| `sys_invitation` | `organization_id`, `sys-invitation.object.ts:255` | better-auth, same call |
| `sys_team` (the default team: `teams: { enabled: true }`, `auth-manager.ts:3579`; created by better-auth `routes/crud-org.mjs:106-126`) | `organization_id`, `sys-team.object.ts:133` | plugin-auth `removeOrganizationAuthStructure`, `organization-delete.ts:240`, from `beforeDeleteOrganization`, `auth-manager.ts:3910` |
| `sys_team_member` | only through `team_id`, `sys-team-member.object.ts:135` | same, by team, before the teams (`organization-delete.ts:246`) |
| `sys_user_permission_set`, **only** grants of `organization_admin` / `organization_admin_no_bypass` | `organization_id`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts:110` | same (`organization-delete.ts:256`); plugin-security's member-delete reconcile did not remove them in time on a booted showcase. Every other grant scoped to the organization counts as a record. |

The exclusion list is `ORGANIZATION_AUTH_STRUCTURE`, `organization-delete.ts:94`.

**3. Rows that outlive the organization, and the references the delete keeps: never NULL, never deleted, never counted.** The set is read from a declaration the objects already carry, never from a list of names (`ObjectQL.outlivesOrganization`, `engine.ts:20042`). Both the engine refusal and the door's count leave it out, and the walk keeps every reference such a row holds (`keepsOrganizationReference`, `engine.ts:20065`, applied at `:19640`):
- **`managedBy: 'append-only'`, the ledgers** (seat decision 6305179819). There are exactly **eight**: `sys_activity`, `sys_audit_log`, `sys_email`, `sys_identity_email`, `sys_job_run`, `sys_metadata_audit`, `sys_approval_action`, `sys_presence`. Four of them hold a reference to an organization:
  - `sys_activity.organization_id`, `sys_email.organization_id` and `sys_approval_action.organization_id`;
  - `sys_audit_log`'s attribution `tenant_id` (`systemFields.tenant: false`, so it is not the tenant column).
- **`managedBy: 'engine-owned'`, rows the platform writes** (seat decision 6307135388). Seventeen of them have an `organization_id`; they are listed in **Round 4** below.
- **An attribution `organization_id` on a tenancy-disabled object** (seat decision 6305996369, B5, the closed rule). Measured over every object registered on a booted showcase with audit, approvals, notifications, mail and sharing composed: **no object matches**. `sys_api_key` is the only tenancy-disabled object with an organization lookup, and its `active_organization_id` is a pointer.
- **Pointers keep `set_null`**: `sys_session.active_organization_id`, `sys_api_key.active_organization_id`, `sys_organization.parent_organization_id`.

**4. Atomic.** `/organization/delete` runs through the same request-level unit of work as subject erasure (`auth-manager.ts:6740`): one engine transaction, rolled back on any 4xx/5xx. On a driver without transactions (Turso remote, `transactionsUnsupported`) the refusals are the guarantee, because both run before the first write: the record count (1), and the Default Organization's guard question (6).

**5. The engine never clears a tenant column.** `refuseOrganizationDeleteWhileOwned` (`engine.ts:20160`, called at `:19624`) refuses a by-id `sys_organization` delete while any tenant-column row outside the cascade set names it. It refuses with `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` and the same `dependents` list, before the walk cascades or clears anything.
- It **counts** each table (`countReferencingRowsOutside`, `:20079`), and never reads rows. The exception is a table the cascade itself deletes rows of, which no platform object is.
- A count is disclosed only when the caller's own identity counts the same (`:20122`).
- A **predicate (`multi`) delete of `sys_organization` is refused** before any hook or write, with `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` naming the by-id route (`organizationPredicateDeleteRefusal`, `:754`, applied at `:20509`): only the by-id path runs this referential pass.
- The door's 409 and the adapter's mapping of the engine refusal both carry `dependents` to the wire (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts:596`, `:650`).
- Nothing in `packages/spec` changes.

**6. The Default Organization.** It is identified by `isDefaultOrganizationTarget` (`organization-delete.ts:216`: slug `default`, else the only organization, never under a wall). That decision is made outside the door's fall-through (`auth-manager.ts:8160`), so a failed lookup refuses instead of handing the delete to better-auth. Its structure is not removed. It is asked two questions, both **in `hooks.before`, before better-auth deletes any member**:
1. The last-administrator guard's question (`auth-manager.ts:8175`), through the guard's own judgement (`LastAdminGuardHandle.judgeOrganizationDelete`, `last-admin-guard.ts:900`, `:1892`, wired in `auth-plugin.ts:1701`). It answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` while the delete would leave no platform administrator.
2. Once the guard admits (an organization-less `admin_full_access` grant, or a verified `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` user, stands), its record count (`defaultOrganizationDeleteRefusal`, `organization-delete.ts:178`, asked at `auth-manager.ts:8184`). This leaves out only the members and invitations better-auth removes, so its teams, its grants and its records count. A refusal is the same `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED`.
- Asked before the vendor's writes, the guard judges the whole change: the organization row **and the members that leave with it** (`pendingFor`, `last-admin-guard.ts:640`). Otherwise an owner's membership of the very organization being deleted would still read as standing.
- On main the 403 arrived after the members and invitations were gone.

### The wire code: `DELETE_RESTRICTED`, not a new `ORGANIZATION_NOT_EMPTY`

A new code needs a row in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, outside the claim's surface. The ledger also refuses a registered synonym of a standard member, and the condition is the standard catalog's `DELETE_RESTRICTED`. Accepted by the seat.

## Review round: contract review 6305988777 (FAIL), answered

- **B1 (CI red).** Two suites pinned the superseded contract and are rewritten to the ruled one, each with a positive control; neither is deleted or weakened.
  - `packages/runtime/src/default-organization-statements.golden.test.ts`, "the Default Organization deleted and recreated". The direct delete is first refused (`DELETE_RESTRICTED`, 409, standing survives). Then the ruled remedy runs: the rows it owns are moved to a holding organization, the organization is deleted and recreated, the rows are moved onto the new one, and the next request reads the new id, as the memo pin asks.
  - `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/business-unit-parent-delete-restrict.test.ts`. "An organization's delete completes, its units stay" becomes "refused while it owns units, `dependents: [{ sys_business_unit, 3 }]`, tree whole", plus the CONTROL "once its units are deleted, leaf to root, the organization deletes".
  - Every test in the tree that deletes an organization was found by grep (objectql, runtime, plugin-auth, plugin-sharing, platform-objects, the hono adapter, dogfood). Their packages' full suites are in **Final readings**.
- **B2.** A predicate delete of `sys_organization` is refused (item 5). Pinned, with a control that another object's multi delete is not caught.
- **B3.** The Default Organization's guard question is asked before the first write (item 6).
  - Seam pins (`last-admin-guard.default-organization.test.ts`): it refuses on the grant anchor; it refuses when the admin's only standing is owning the Default Organization, which needs the member companion (ablated: without it, exactly that case goes red); it admits when another administrator stands elsewhere.
  - Door pin (federated dogfood (e)): an engine `beforeDelete` recorder on `sys_member` and `sys_invitation` sees **no delete attempted** by the refused request, and members, invitations and teams are unchanged. That does not depend on the transaction. A positive control on the 200 delete in the same file proves the recorder fires.
  - The changeset's no-transactions sentence is kept, now true for both refusals.
- **B4.** Every lookup to `sys_organization` on an append-only ledger is kept (item 3). Pinned in objectql (an append-only object's non-tenant lookup keeps naming it, with no write) and in dogfood (b) (every `sys_audit_log` row whose `tenant_id` named the organization still does after the delete).
- **B5.** The closed rule is implemented as written and pinned in objectql (a tenancy-disabled object's `organization_id` is kept and not counted; a pointer is still cleared). It touches no object in this tree. `sys_approval_request` is walled, so the decision's premise about it did not hold. Decision 6307135388 settles it (**Round 4**).
- **B6.** The changeset names the seed replay and its remedy. Measured on a walled `os serve` (showcase + `@objectstack/organizations`): a fresh organization owns **132 rows in 19 tables**:
  - `showcase_account` 14, `showcase_announcement` 2, `showcase_business_unit` 9, `showcase_category` 4, `showcase_client_brief` 2, `showcase_contact` 32, `showcase_expense_line` 13;
  - `showcase_expense_report` 4, `showcase_field_zoo` 2, `showcase_inquiry` 3, `showcase_invoice` 12, `showcase_invoice_line` 5, `showcase_preference` 1, `showcase_product` 4;
  - `showcase_project` 5, `showcase_project_membership` 3, `showcase_task` 10, `showcase_team` 2, `sys_business_unit` 5.
- **B8.** The adapter carries `dependents` through to the wire 409 (item 5). Pinned in `objectql-adapter.test.ts`, a withheld count staying absent.
- **B9.** The engine refusal counts (item 5). Pinned: refusing an organization that owns 5 rows issues no row read of the owning table.
- **B7, B10, B11.** Accepted as declared. The ledger count is corrected: eight objects, not nine.

## Measurements (counts only)

**Upgrade fixtures**, re-measured on `e184b513c`, after the engine-owned exemption; the figures are identical to round 3's (walled boot over each, `AuditPlugin` composed). Three door-created organizations per fixture: untouched; holding one `sys_business_unit`; holding one record.

| Fixture | `sys_team.organization_id` NOT NULL | Untouched | With a business unit | With a record |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ceremonied 18.0 (after `os migrate organization-ownership --apply`: complete, 0 blocking) | yes | `200`; organization, members, invitations, teams, team members, grants all 0; `sys_activity` naming it 4 → 7 (kept, plus the delete's own), 0 NULL | `409` `sys_business_unit (1)`, every count unchanged | `409` `showcase_category (1)`, every count unchanged |
| `fixture-18.0.0` | no | the same | the same | the same |

After that delete, on the ceremonied database: the ceremony re-run answers `complete: true`, `blocking: 0` (its post-check holds only `organization_id IS NULL` rows), and HEAD boots it through `OrganizationOwnershipBootGuardPlugin` (which decides on one field of the `sys_migration` marker). `check:tenant-audit-census` is a static count of source. A REST read over the kept ledger rows answers `200`. The lifecycle sweep's dangling-reference audit only reports, into its sweep report.

**Walled `os serve`**, re-measured on `e184b513c` (`OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated`, `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`, `OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY=invite-only`, a scratch copy of the showcase declaring `@objectstack/organizations`, the RUNNER.md recipe; `Organizations`, `Security` and `Audit` mounted):
- health `200`, sign-in `200`, 0 error lines;
- a fresh organization: `409` naming the 19 tables / 132 rows above, every count unchanged;
- after the operator's remedy (its records deleted over `DELETE /api/v1/data/...`, three passes for ordering): `200`, with organization, members, teams and grants 0;
- read from the databases: `sys_activity.organization_id` 312 rows still name the deleted organization, 0 NULL; `sys_audit_log.tenant_id` 312 rows still name it. `sys_approval_request`, `sys_setting`, `sys_record_share` and `sys_notification` hold no row naming it on this boot, and none with a NULL `organization_id`. The 11 audit rows with a NULL `tenant_id` are deployment-level rows written at boot and by the delete itself, not cleared ones; dogfood (b) pins that every row naming the organization before the delete still does after it.

**R1** fresh `pnpm dev -- --fresh` (showcase, `single`): health `200`, seeded-admin sign-in `200`, 0 error lines; Default Organization delete `403`, members 3 → 3, records 14 → 14 (measured last round; the Default Organization path is re-pinned this round by dogfood (e)).
**R2** `upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts`: see **Final readings**.

**Main baseline** (`e4d604efd`): Default Organization delete `403` with `sys_member` 1 → 0.

## Round 5: delta review 6308041940 (R1 blocking, R2, R3), answered

- **R1 (blocking): the Default Organization's delete is counted before the first write.** Once the last-administrator guard admits the delete, `hooks.before` asks `defaultOrganizationDeleteRefusal` (`organization-delete.ts:178`, asked at `auth-manager.ts:8184`). It counts every table holding rows that name the organization, leaving out only the members and invitations better-auth removes (`VENDOR_REMOVED_ON_DELETE`). Its teams, its grants and its records count, since plugin-auth removes none of its structure. A refusal is the same `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED`, before better-auth's first write, so a driver without transactions no longer gets a partial delete on this path.
  - Pinned in federated dogfood under a config anchor: the admin is named in `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` and verified, so the guard admits.
    - The response is `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED`. It names the Default Organization's records and does not list `sys_member` or `sys_invitation`.
    - An engine recorder on `sys_member` and `sys_invitation` sees **no delete attempted**.
    - Members, invitations, teams and the organization row are unchanged.
  - Ablated (the count skipped for the Default Organization): exactly that pin goes red, and the other 5 stay green.
  - At the seam (`organization-delete.test.ts`): the exclusion is exactly members and invitations, and no organization-admin grant is subtracted.
  - Re-read and corrected so they hold:
    - the changeset's opening paragraph (`single` deployments) and its no-transactions bullet;
    - a new Default Organization bullet;
    - the contract notes in `organization-delete.ts`, items 3 and the closing paragraph, and `isDefaultOrganizationTarget`'s doc.
- **R2: the organization counts carry none of the caller's tenant scope.** `countReferencingRowsOutside` and `organizationOwnedRowCounts` now count under `organizationCountContext` (`engine.ts:20109`). That context is system identity, keeping only the request's transaction (so the count sees the request's own writes) and its trace. Ordinary reference probes keep `referenceCheckContext` and the caller's scope.
  - Pinned in objectql with a tenant-scoping middleware. CONTROL: the caller's own count for the organization reads 0 under it.
    - `organizationOwnedRowCounts` under a foreign `tenantId` still counts 2.
    - The engine refusal still refuses a caller scoped to another organization.
  - Ablated (back to `referenceCheckContext`): both pins go red.
- **R3: deciding whether the target is the Default Organization is outside the fall-through.** `isDefaultOrganizationTarget` runs after the `try` (`auth-manager.ts:8160`), so a lookup that fails there refuses instead of handing the delete to better-auth.
  - Pinned in federated dogfood. A non-default organization the admin owns is made active, and the organization count fails (a middleware on `sys_organization`). Under these conditions:
    - the request is refused (≥ 400);
    - a recorder on the session's active-organization write (better-auth's first) and on member, invitation and organization deletes sees nothing attempted;
    - the organization and its member are unchanged.
    - CONTROL: with the lookup back, the same organization deletes with `200`.
  - Ablated (the decision moved back into the `try`): the pin goes red, because better-auth's session write was attempted.
  - Before this round the pin recorded deletes only, and stayed green under the same ablation, because the last-administrator guard's own member hook threw first. The session write is what makes it discriminating.

## Round 4: seat decision 6307135388 (option B), answered

**Exempt by declaration.** `managedBy: 'engine-owned'` joins `managedBy: 'append-only'` in `ObjectQL.outlivesOrganization` (`engine.ts:20042`), which is the one predicate behind all three of these:
- the engine refusal (`refuseOrganizationDeleteWhileOwned`);
- the door's count (`organizationOwnedRowCounts`, which plugin-auth asks);
- the walk's kept references (`keepsOrganizationReference`).

No list of names is involved. Such rows are not counted. They are kept, and go on naming the deleted organization: never NULL, never deleted.

**The 17 engine-owned objects with an `organization_id`**, measured over every object registered on a booted showcase (audit, approvals, automation, messaging, mail and sharing composed: 109 objects). The other fourteen of the 31 engine-owned objects carry no organization reference and are untouched: the `sys_metadata*` family (with `sys_metadata_activation`), `sys_platform_setting*`, `sys_migration*`, `sys_secret`, `sys_flow_dispatch`, `sys_flow_credential`, `sys_job`, `sys_job_queue`, `sys_scim_connection_credential`.

| Object | What writes its rows |
|---|---|
| `sys_approval_request` | plugin-approvals' approval service: one row per submission, advanced by the flow until it completes. |
| `sys_approval_approver` | the approval service: the normalized pending-approver rows behind the inbox query, one per approver per step. |
| `sys_approval_token` | the approval service: the single-use tokens behind actionable approval links. |
| `sys_automation_run` | service-automation's flow runner: paused runs waiting to resume, and the history of finished runs. |
| `sys_notification` | service-messaging: one row per notification event the platform sent. |
| `sys_notification_receipt` | service-messaging: per recipient × channel. Read state is set by the recipient through the messaging API. |
| `sys_notification_delivery` | service-messaging: the durable per-recipient × channel delivery outbox. |
| `sys_http_delivery` | service-messaging: one row per outgoing webhook or flow HTTP call, with its delivery status. |
| `sys_mailbox` | **see below.** The mailbox sync writes its IMAP cursor. |
| `sys_mail_message` | service-mailbox's sync and ingest: inbound mail mirrored from a mailbox. |
| `sys_mail_association` | service-mailbox's ingest: links a mirrored message to the records it matched. |
| `sys_audience_binding_suggestion` | a package's suggestion, written by the platform when the package is installed. A `manage_metadata` holder accepts or dismisses it. |
| `sys_record_share` | plugin-sharing: rule grants (`source = 'rule'`) written and reconciled by the sharing-rule evaluator, and **see below** for `source = 'manual'`. |
| `sys_share_link` | **see below.** |
| `sys_import_job` | the import service: the state, progress and history of a bulk import. |
| `sys_setting` | **see below.** |
| `sys_setting_audit` | `SettingsService`: the audit trail of every settings change. |

**Rows that are an administrator's or a user's own act, with a door other than the data API.** These were named for a separate decision. **Decision 6307815346 settles them: the declaration decides, with no per-table exceptions, so all are kept, and it amends 6305179819 on settings.**
1. **`sys_setting`** (organization-level settings values). An administrator sets them through `SettingsService.set` (the Setup settings pages), and `resetNamespace` removes them. Decision 6305179819 said "settings stay records". Under 6307135388's rule, a `sys_setting` row no longer refuses the delete. If 6305179819 meant `sys_setting`, the two decisions now conflict on this table. (If it meant organization-level settings stored elsewhere, there is no conflict: no other object named for settings has an `organization_id`.)
2. **`sys_mailbox`.** It is a mailbox's identity (address, owner), and only `manage_mailboxes` holders can read the directory. No code in this tree creates one; tests insert them directly, so in a deployment the operator provisions them. It is administrator configuration with no delete door.
3. **`sys_record_share` with `source = 'manual'`, and `sys_share_link`.** A user creates them through `POST /data/:object/:id/shares` and the share-link service's `createLink`, and revokes them through the same service: `revokeLink` sets `revoked_at` and keeps the row. Decision 6307135388 names shares as engine-derived, so they are exempt as decided.

**Pinned.**
- objectql (`engine-organization-delete-refusal.test.ts`):
  - an organization whose only rows are an engine-owned approval request and its append-only actions deletes, and both are kept naming it with no write;
  - CONTROL: beside them, a record still refuses, and only the record is named.
  - Ablated (`engine-owned` removed from the predicate): exactly these two pins go red, and the other 15 stay green.
- dogfood (`organization-delete-refuse-nonempty.dogfood.test.ts`), on a booted showcase:
  - an organization created through the door, holding one real `sys_approval_request` and its two `sys_approval_action` rows, deletes with `200`;
  - the request and both actions are unchanged and still name it;
  - 0 rows in either table have a NULL `organization_id`.

**Changeset.** It says that engine-owned and append-only rows outlive the organization and go on naming it, and it lists what engine-owned covers. The **Fix** bullet no longer lists settings values among the records.

**Merged `main`** (`3b3830ca2`, which includes `62bc12930`) with a merge commit. It merged cleanly.

## File surface

Inside the claim: `packages/objectql/src/**`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/**`, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/**`, one changeset. Outside it:
- **Accepted by the seat for generated artefacts only:** `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md` (`tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`), `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (`check-engine-double-contract --write`).
- **This round, by the review's B1:** `packages/runtime/src/default-organization-statements.golden.test.ts` and `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/business-unit-parent-delete-restrict.test.ts`, the two suites the review named.

No `packages/spec/src/**`, no `docs/adr/**`, no governed surface.

## Tests

- `packages/objectql/src/engine-organization-delete-refusal.test.ts`:
  - the refusal, nothing written, a declared `set_null` tenant column refused;
  - controls: an empty organization deletes, a pointer is cleared, a missing table refuses nothing;
  - ledgers: kept, a record still refusing beside one, the count excluding them;
  - B4 (non-tenant ledger lookup kept), B5 (tenancy-disabled attribution kept and not counted, pointer cleared);
  - B2 (predicate delete refused, control);
  - B9 (no row read while refusing);
  - R2 (round 5): the counts under a foreign tenant scope, through a tenant-scoping middleware with its CONTROL;
  - `organizationOwnedRowCounts`.
  - engine-owned (round 4): an approval request and its actions are kept and the organization deletes; a record beside them still refuses.
- `packages/objectql/src/federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts`: census rows for the new tenant-column readers.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/organization-delete.test.ts`, `last-admin-guard.default-organization.test.ts` (B3), `objectql-adapter.test.ts` (B8).
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/organization-delete-refuse-nonempty.dogfood.test.ts`, booted with `AuditPlugin`:
  - (a) (c): a refused delete changes nothing;
  - (b): the empty delete, with `sys_activity` and `sys_audit_log` rows kept;
  - an organization holding only an approval request and its actions deletes, and they are kept (round 4);
  - a business-unit-only refusal;
  - (d): the engine refusal;
  - the vendor-refused caller, and the remedy.
- `organization-delete-federated-fixture.dogfood.test.ts`: nothing names a deleted organization; (e) the Default Organization's 403 with no member or invitation delete attempted, plus its recorder control; (round 5) R1, the Default Organization admitted by the guard on a config anchor and refused 409 with no member or invitation delete attempted; R3, a failed Default Organization lookup refusing before better-auth's first write, with its CONTROL; the count skipping the federated anchor.
- `org-record-admin-reach.dogfood.test.ts`: structure gone, no orphan, 409 control.
- The B1 rewrites above.
- **Ablations** (restored to HEAD's blob):
  - the engine refusal call replaced: its 3 pins red;
  - the door gate inverted (rebuilt, dist preflight): dogfood (a) red;
  - the guard's member companion deleted: exactly the membership case red, 8 others green.
  - `engine-owned` removed from `outlivesOrganization`: exactly the two round-4 pins red, 15 others green.
  - Round 5:
    - the Default Organization's count skipped: R1's pin red, 5 others green;
    - `organizationCountContext` back to `referenceCheckContext`: both R2 pins red;
    - the Default Organization decision moved back into the `try`: R3's pin red.
  - A first attempt at the last one used an empty replacement, which the tool refuses, and it restored the file to HEAD before that work was committed. It was re-applied from the edit scripts, committed, then ablated.

## Verification on the head (139abc45a)

Every reading below was taken on 139abc45a, which is `e184b513c` plus the round-5 commits `e40aea862` and `139abc45a`, rebuilt.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/dogfood^...'` | exit 0 |
| objectql tests | 452 files, 8526 passed |
| plugin-auth tests | 176 files, 3356 passed, 10 skipped |
| runtime tests | 432 files, 6794 passed, 19 skipped |
| plugin-sharing tests | 53 files, 1200 passed |

| hono tests | 12 files, 225 passed |
| plugin-approvals tests | 93 files, 1208 passed |
| typecheck: objectql, plugin-auth, runtime, plugin-sharing, dogfood | exit 0 each |
| dogfood organization files (refuse-nonempty, federated-fixture, org-record-admin-reach, organization-update-door) | 4 files, 32 passed |
